summary: The session-manager removal is mostly clean: stale references are effectively gone, the docs have been updated consistently, and the targeted tests pass. I would not approve this yet because the new `--task` transport moves full prompts onto the process command line, and the timeout path in `one-shot-runner.ts` can still leave `api-task-runner` children running after the parent reports a timeout.

findings.description: Lines 243-251 now pass the entire task text as `--task <prompt>` when spawning `api-task-runner.ts`. That introduces two regressions compared with the old HTTP-body transport: prompt contents are exposed in process listings (`ps`, `/proc/.../cmdline`) and large review/implementation prompts can fail at OS argv limits (`E2BIG` on Unix, much lower limits on Windows). The new CLI contract in `api-task-runner.ts` and the updated CLAUDE/SKILL docs all reinforce this path, so API-provider tasks need a stdin/temp-file/pipe transport instead of argv.

In the timeout branch at lines 287-293, the parent sends `SIGTERM`, schedules a `SIGKILL` with `setTimeout`, and immediately returns. `main()` then calls `process.exit()`, so the grace-period timer never gets a chance to fire. If `api-task-runner` ignores or does not promptly handle `SIGTERM`, the supposedly timed-out child process can survive as an orphan and keep consuming resources or modifying the workspace after the caller has already reported failure.

The updated tests validate exit-code mapping, but they never exercise the real hang/cleanup branch even though `mockApiDeps()` has `shouldHang` support. There is also no coverage for oversized task payloads passed via `--task`. That gap is why the orphaned-child timeout bug and the argv-size/process-list regression both slip through while the suite still passes.
